THIS MFA FILED U/S 173(1) OF MV ACT, PRAYING TO CALL FOR THE RECORDS AND SET ASIDE THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD PASSED BY THE MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS TRIBUNAL NO.III, VIJAYAPUR, AT: VIJAYAPUR IN MVC NO.1344/2015 DATED 28.10.2016 BY MODIFYING THE IMPUGNED ORDER AND BE PLEASED TO ALLOW THE CLAIM PETITION BY GRANTING THE RELIEF AS PRAYED FAR BY THE APPELLANT AND ETC.

THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE N.S.SANJAY GOWDA  ORAL JUDGMENT (PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE N.S.SANJAY GOWDA)
1.
Being aggrieved by the award of Rs.3,37,400/-, both the insurer as well as the claimants are in appeal.

2. It was the case of the claimant that while he was riding his motorcycle on 07.07.2015, he was hit by a tipper lorry belonging to one Javeed (respondent No.1 before the Tribunal), as a result of which,
he sustained serious injuries and was initially admitted at Tanga Multi Speciality Hospital, Vijaypur and thereafter shifted to Chandrapattan Hospital where he underwent treatment.
He therefore sought for compensation for injuries suffered by him which had resulted in a disability.
The owner of the tipper lorry, though served and represented by a counsel, did not choose to file his objections.
4. The insurer however, filed objections denying all the averments including the occurrence of the accident.

5. The Tribunal has however come to the conclusion that, an accident did occur and this was due to the negligence of the driver of the tipper lorry against whom the police had registered a criminal case and it also laid a charge sheet.
The Tribunal has thereafter assessed the disability at 8% and has taken the notional income at Rs.6,000/- and awarded a total sum of Rs.3,37,400/-.

sentences.text: 3 6. The case put forth by the insurer regarding the occurrence of the accident is that, the insured tipper lorry was implicated in order to secure compensation.
In order to substantiate this, reliance is sought to be placed on the medical bills.
It is argued that, according to the three medical bills produced at Ex.P-6, P-75 and P-76, it can be NC: 2024:KHC-K:6850 gathered that the case put forward by the claimant was fictitious.
It is stated that, as per Ex.P-6, Chandrapattan Hospital has issued a bill in which it is stated that the claimant was admitted from 07.07.2015 to 23.07.2015.

It is also stated that the claimant has produced Ex.P-75 and P-76 pertaining to Wanless Hospital in which it is indicated that the claimant was admitted from 08.07.2015 to 10.07.2015 and from 11.07.2015 to 14.07.2015.
7.

It is therefore contended that, the claimant could not have been admitted to two hospitals at the same time for the same injuries and thus the entire story put forth was false and consequently, it had to be held that the involvement of the vehicle was also fabricated.
8.
The Trial court records reveal that a summons was issued to Dr.Anil S.Chandrapattan to produce the case sheet pertaining to the treatment given to the claimant.
The records contain the original case sheet.
It appears that it has not been marked as an exhibit.
This case sheet indicates that the claimant was admitted on 07.07.2015 NC: 2024:KHC-K:6850 and there is an endorsement in the case sheet that ICU care was required for a period of seven days.
Thereafter, there is no entry till 16.07.2015.

This indicates that the claimant was not treated at Chandrapattan Hospital from 07.07.2015 to 16.07.2015.
9.
Ex . P-76, the bill issued by Wanless hospital indicates that the claimant was admitted in the ICU from 08.07.2015 to 10.07.2015 and Ex.P-75
indicates that he was admitted from 11.07.2015 to 14.07.2015.

If these three bills are read in conjunction with the case sheet that is available wherein,
it is stated that, the claimant was required ICU care for seven days, it becomes clear that, the claimant was in Chandrapattan Hospital till 07.07.2015 and at Wanless Hospital from 08.07.2015 to 14.07.2015 and subsequently returned to Chandrapattan Hospital from 16.07.2015.
The said fact would clearly establish that there is no falsity in the case put forth by the claimant to doubt the occurrence of the accident itself.

As far as the involvement of the vehicle is concerned, the owner of the vehicle, though entered appearance through a counsel did not contest the occurrence of the accident and the involvement of his vehicle.
The insurer did not reduce any evidence to establish that the accident did not occur.

The insurer ought to have adduced evidence of independent witnesses or ought to have summoned the driver of the tipper and subjected to cross-examination to elicit whether an accident did or did not occur.
This having not been done, it is not open for the insurer to contend that the vehicle that, it had insured was not involved in the accident.

Furthermore, the police records indicate that the tipper lorry was involved in the accident and in the light of these facts, the argument of the insurer that there was no accident and that the vehicle was implicated, cannot be accepted.
The appeal of the insurer is therefore dismissed.

sentences.text: As far as the claim for enhancement by the claimant is concerned, it is noticed that the claimant according to NC: 2024:KHC-K:6850 the medical certificate which was produced, Ex.P-4 had suffered a fracture of left femur with crush injury and he was also put on a ventilator for a case of pulmonary embolism.
The indoor patient bill of Wanless Hospital also indicates that he was put on a ventilator for which incubation charges have been collected.

In the light of this evidence, in my view,
the assertion of disability at 8% is on the lower side and would be appropriate to determine the disability at 15%.
12.
As the claimant was aged 23 years, a multiplier of '18' would have to be applied.
The Tribunal has taken the notional income of the claimant at Rs.6,000/- per month.
Since for the accidents of the year 2015, the KSLSA has determined a sum of Rs.8,000/-, it would be appropriate to adopt the said sum.

Consequently, towards 'loss of future earning', the claimant would be entitled to sum of Rs.2,59,200/- (Rs.8,000x12x18x15%).
13.

The Tribunal has refused to accept the medical bill issued by Chandrapattan Hospital for sum of Rs.4,02,100/-
NC: 2024:KHC-K:6850 on the ground that the case sheet was not produced by the claimant and hence there may be an understanding between the hospital and the claimant to issue a bill for a higher sum to claim compensation.
14. This observation would be factually incorrect since the original record indicates that, the entire case sheet was summoned by the Tribunal itself and the same is also found in the records.
This case sheet, to which reference has been made earlier, indicates that the claimant was hospitalized on 07.07.2015 and from 16.07.2015 till he was discharged on 23.07.2015.
The case sheet also indicates that the claimant was hospitalized was subject to a surgical procedure.
15. In this view of the matter, the rejection of Ex.P-6 would not be correct.
Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to sum of Rs.4,02,100/- as indicated in Ex.P-6 apart from the sum of Rs.1,45,300/- already awarded by the Tribunal.

The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.30,000/- towards pain and suffering and Rs.8,000/-
towards loss of amenities.

Having regard to the fact that the claimant was incubated and was hospitalized for more than 15 days, and also taking into consideration that he has suffered 15%
disability, it would be appropriate to award a sum Rs.75,000/- towards 'pain and suffering' and Rs.40,000/- towards 'loss of amenities'.
17.

The laid up period of six months taken by the Tribunal is accepted and since the income is not determined at Rs.8,000/-, he would be entitled to sum of Rs.48,000/- (Rs.8,000x6months) as against Rs.36,000/-.
